newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: EU says it has great confidence in Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: EU says it has great confidence in Guatemala.

text.p: A European Union official said on Friday the group's $226 million contribution to supporting peace in Guatemala reflects its historic level of confidence in the country's progress.

"For the first time the European Union will cooperate in defining legal property rights and establishing a national property register," Manuel Marin, vice president of the European Commission said in a ceremony at the national palace.
"This implies a level of confidence that until now we had not gained with any other country," he said.
In Guatemala, questions of land ownership are fundamentally political, Marin noted. In the past, outside involvement in such basic affairs of state was seen as foreign interference, he said.

Marin and Guatemalan Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein signed a joint declaration essentially ratifying a Jan. 21 agreement under which the European Union will provide $200 million Ecus ($226 million) through the year 2000.

Under the declaration, international support focuses on demobilization of the rebel and government armies and their incorporation into civilian life; establishment of a national property register; decentralization of the state; citizen security; strengthening the justice system.

The international community as a whole has promised $1.9 billion in loans, gifts and technical assistance to support the peace agreement signed on Dec. 29 that ended 36 years of civil war between the government and leftist rebels.
